# Adjudication Task — Chapter 357

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃357화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|평온한 표정과 걸음걸이. 깨끗한 황색 장삼.
  6|
  7|그는 홀로 이질적인 존재였고, 사천당문을 가득 메운 죽음의 기운이 범접할 수 있는 유일한 사람이었다.
  8|
  9|“기껏해야 한 줌밖에 안 되는 놈들이다. 밀어붙여라!”
 10|
 11|“끝까지 싸워라. 우리는 대 사천당문이다!”
 12|
 13|와아아아!
 14|
 15|지축을 떨어 울리는 거대한 함성과 함께 두 개의 파도가 부딪쳤다. 비명과 함성이 뒤섞이고 자욱한 피 안개가 맺혀 간다.
 16|
 17|목숨을 도외시한 치열한 전투. 그만큼 승패가 갈리는 것 또한 순식간이었다.
 18|
 19|“포위하라! 단 한 놈도 살려 두어서는 안 된다!”
 20|
 21|“크아아악!”
 22|
 23|흑의(黑衣)로 이루어진 검은 파도가 녹색 파도를 집어삼켰다.
 24|
 25|파도가 휩쓴 자리에 포말처럼 남은 것은 녹의(綠衣)를 걸친 시신들이었다.
 26|
 27|백여 장 밖에서 이 모든 상황을 바라보던 그, 서천마군이 문득 입을 열었다.
 28|
 29|“끝났군.”
 30|
 31|물러서지 않고 맞서는 결기는 존중할 만하나, 애당초 중과부적(衆寡不敵)의 싸움이었다.
 32|
 33|사천당문의 근간이라 할 수 있는 독과 암기마저 제대로 힘을 발휘하지 못하는 상황.
 34|
 35|전투는, 아니 이 전쟁은 암천의 승리다.
 36|
 37|“약속은 지키지 못할 것 같군. 미안하네, 당 가주.”
 38|
 39|인간은 절박할수록 판단력이 흐려지는 법. 당사독도 예외는 아니었다.
 40|
 41|당가의 명맥을 잇게 해 준다는 조건으로 원하던 대답을 얻어 낸 서천마군이 취한 행동은 간단하고, 잔인했다.
 42|
 43|당장 목숨을 끊는 대신 사천당문이 내려다보이는 언덕 위 나무에 그를 앉혀 놓은 것이다.
 44|
 45|숨이 끊길 때까지 자신의 가문이 멸망하는 것을 지켜볼 수 있도록.
 46|
 47|“모든 것은 천주의 뜻대로.”
 48|
 49|투둑, 투두둑.
 50|
 51|어느새 빗방울을 떨어트리는 하늘을 바라보던 서천마군이 신형을 돌렸다.
 52|
 53|시커먼 아가리를 쩍 벌리고 있는 동혈(洞穴) 입구. 쓰러진 화로 옆에 웬 곱사등이 노인 하나가 눈을 부릅뜬 채 죽어 있었다.
 54|
 55|서천마군의 흥미를 끈 것은 노인의 몸에 새겨진 상흔이었다.
 56|
 57|‘흑혈검법(黑血劍法).’
 58|
 59|흑혈검법은 암천의 무인들에게만 허락된 검법.
 60|
 61|선객들의 정체를 알아차린 서천마군은 지하로 향하는 돌계단을 따라 내려갔다.
 62|
 63|계단에는 핏물과 진흙이 뒤섞인 발자국들이 선명하게 남아 있었다. 적어도 스물 이상의 수하들이 그보다 앞서 이곳을 방문했음이 틀림없었다.
 64|
 65|그리고 아마도…….
 66|
 67|‘모두 죽었겠지.’
 68|
 69|내려간 흔적은 있어도 올라온 흔적은 없다.
 70|
 71|지하 뇌옥에 진입하자 짐작은 확신으로 변했다.
 72|
 73|피로 얼룩진 인생을 살았던 서천마군이다. 어두컴컴한 복도에 남아 있는 전투의 열기, 악취에 덮인 비릿한 혈향(血香)을 느낄 수 있었다.
 74|
 75|누구의 짓일까, 서천마군은 벽면에 튄 미세한 핏방울을 보며 생각했다.
 76|
 77|‘솜씨가 좋군. 제대로 된 저항도 하지 못하고 당했어.’
 78|
 79|사천당문이 풍전등화의 위기에 처한 지금, 당문의 고수들이 외인들을 지키기 위해 이곳에 있을 리는 없다.
 80|
 81|당사독의 말이 사실이라면 지금 지하 뇌옥에 남아 있는 자는 셋.
 82|
 83|신의는 있으나 마나 한 전력이고 화왕 적천강은 의식을 회복하지도 못했으니, 남은 사람은 한 명뿐이다.
 84|
 85|‘산서잠룡 진태경.’
 86|
 87|문득 혈주가 진태경을 두고 했던 말이 생각났다.
 88|
 89|천하에서 가장 건방지고, 끈질기며, 간이 배 밖으로 튀어나온 어린놈.
 90|
 91|어째서인지 그는 제 팔을 잘라 낸 검성이나 화왕보다 진태경을 더 죽이고 싶어 했다.
 92|
 93|‘혈주를 상대로 살아남을 정도의 실력은 있다, 이건가.’
 94|
 95|그러나 진태경에게 두 번의 요행은 없을 것이다.
 96|
 97|검성은 이 자리에 없고 화왕 역시 전투 불능의 상태.
 98|
 99|서천마군은 독 안에 든 쥐새끼들을 손쉽게 붙잡아 귀환할 생각이었다.
100|
101|‘놈들이 가진 만독지환과 함께 말이지.’
102|
103|철벅, 철벅.
104|
105|여유롭게 걸음을 옮기던 서천마군의 신형이 우뚝 멈췄다.
106|
107|어느새 천장으로부터 이어진 단단한 돌벽이 그를 가로막고 있었다.
108|
109|“허, 참. 복잡하게도 지어 놨군.”
110|
111|물끄러미 벽을 바라보던 서천마군이 손을 그러모았다. 검붉은 안개가 그의 팔을 휘감으며 주먹을 감싼다.
112|
113|고오오오옹.
114|
115|모든 것은 순식간에 일어났다.
116|
117|기의 발현, 압축, 그리고 폭발. 권강(拳罡)의 앞을 가로막을 수 있는 것은 아무것도 없었다.
118|
119|쿠구구구궁!
120|
121|부수고, 무너지고, 흔들린다.
122|
123|강대한 기의 집약체는 일직선으로 뻗어 나가며 수십 개의 벽을 관통했다. 천장에서는 종유석이 우박처럼 쏟아져 내렸고 자욱한 먼지구름이 피어올랐다.
124|
125|‘한결 낫군.’
126|
127|다음 순간.
128|
129|자신이 만든 광경을 바라보던 서천마군이 문득 입을 열었다.
130|
131|“이만 나오지 그러나.”
132|
133|대답 대신 돌아온 것은 강렬한 파공성이었다.
134|
135|퍼엉!
136|
137|갈라지는 먼지구름 사이, 자신의 목을 향해 날아든 비수를 낚아챈 서천마군이 빙긋 웃었다.
138|
139|“자네가 진태경인가?”
140|
141|“알면서 뭘 물어.”
142|
143|저벅, 저벅.
144|
145|먼지구름을 헤치며 걸어온 훤칠한 체구의 청년, 진태경이 덤덤한 눈빛으로 서천마군을 응시했다.
146|
147|
148|
149|* * *
150|
151|
152|
153|나는 덤덤해 보이려고 애썼다.
154|
155|싸움은 기세가 절반은 먹고 들어간다. 상대가 나보다 약해 보인다고 해서 방심하면 안 되고, 강해 보인다고 해서 주눅 들어서도 안 된다.
156|
157|특히…… 지금처럼 진짜배기 강자를 만났을 때는 더더욱.
158|
159|‘뭐 이런 괴물 같은 놈이.’
160|
161|내심 혀를 내두르며 눈앞의 중년인을 바라봤다.
162|
163|모세가 지팡이로 바다를 갈랐다면, 그는 일권(一拳)으로 지하 뇌옥에 또 다른 길을 만들었다.
164|
165|그뿐인가, 미소 띤 얼굴로 서 있는 모습은 평온 그 자체였다.
166|
167|‘풍기는 냄새 자체가 달라.’
168|
169|혈주가 대놓고 미친놈이었다면, 눈앞의 이 중년인은 존재 자체만으로도 위험한 인간이다.
170|
171|둘의 무공은 엇비슷할지 몰라도 종류가 달랐다.
172|
173|“자네 얘기는 많이 들었네. 듣던 대로 재밌는 청년이로군.”
174|
175|나는 백염(白炎)의 창날을 비스듬하게 늘어트리며 대꾸했다.
176|
177|“내가 또 한 재미 하지.”
178|
179|“예의가 없다고도 하더군.”
180|
181|“사람 잘못 봤네. 내 별명이 예의범절이거든.”
182|
183|“글쎄, 자네를 조금 더 겪어 봐야 알겠지만, 내 지인이 전해 준 바로는 그렇다네.”
184|
185|“친구 없어 보이는데. 지인 누구?”
186|
187|중년인의 입가에 맺힌 웃음이 짙어졌다.
188|
189|“혈주(血主).”
190|
191|“……!”
192|
193|“그가 자네를 매우 보고 싶어 하더군.”
194|
195|“난 그 시부럴 새끼 꼴도 보기 싫은데.”
196|
197|“청풍, 그 젊은이와 똑같은 말을 하는군. 어조는 다르지만.”
198|
199|이놈, 이미 청풍을 만났구나.
200|
201|그런데도 이 자리에 있다는 건…….
202|
203|나도 모르게 안면 근육이 딱딱하게 경직되는 것을 느끼며 입을 열었다.
204|
205|“너, 혹시.”
206|
207|중년인이 웃으며 손을 내저었다.
208|
209|“걱정할 것 없네. 죽이지는 않을 테니까. 자네와 청풍, 그리고 화왕도 무사히 살려서 데려갈 생각이거든.”
210|
211|나는 어안이 벙벙한 얼굴로 물었다.
212|
213|“데려간다고?”
214|
215|“말했잖나. 혈주가 보고 싶어 한다고. 그러니 적어도 그전까지는 무사할 걸세.”
216|
217|“…….”
218|
219|“물론 그 후는 혈주에게 달렸겠지만 말일세.”
220|
221|중년인은 좋은 소식 두 개와 나쁜 소식을 하나씩 전해 주었다.
222|
223|전자는 청풍의 생존 소식과 혈주가 이 자리에 없다는 것이고, 후자는 이 싸움에서 진다면 혈주와 단체 정모를 하게 될 거라는 사실이다.
224|
225|물론 곱창에 소주 한잔 걸치고 헤어질 확률은 제로에 가깝다.
226|
227|‘대신 내가 곱창이 될 확률이 오십 퍼센트쯤 되겠지.’
228|
229|나머지 오십 퍼센트는 막창이 될 확률이고.
230|
231|빌어먹을, 생각만 해도 아주 입안에 침이 고이네.
232|
233|마른침을 꿀꺽 삼킨 나는 중년인을 위아래로 훑었다.
234|
235|암천에서도 최고위층으로 짐작되는 혈주를 ‘지인’이라고 부를 수 있는 자. 단 일 수로 이만한 파괴력을 보여주는 무력.
236|
237|머릿속에 한 사람의 별호가 떠올랐다.
238|
239|“서천마군, 맞지?”
240|
241|“아, 그러고 보니 아직 내 소개를 하지 않았군. 만나서 반갑네.”
242|
243|반갑기는 개뿔이.
244|
245|나는 서천마군의 멀쩡한 두 팔을 바라보며 중얼거렸다.
246|
247|“외팔이라고 들었는데.”
248|
249|“그랬지. 열흘 전까지는.”
250|
251|“뭐?”
252|
253|“다시 붙였거든. 본래 내 것이 아니라 아직 움직임이 영 시원치 않으니, 기왕 해볼 거라면 왼팔을 노려 보게.”
254|
255|“……!”
256|
257|이 자식 도대체 뭐지?
258|
259|봉합 수술쯤이야 어찌어찌 가능하다 쳐도, 팔을 컴퓨터 부품처럼 갈아 끼우다니.
260|
261|심지어 피부색이 미묘하게 다른 걸 빼면 그 움직임이 자연스럽기 그지없다.
262|
263|‘이게 가능하다고? 그것도 고작 열흘 만에?’
264|
265|도무지 이해가 가지 않았지만, 놀라움과 의문은 잠시 접어 둬야 했다.
266|
267|그보다는 녀석의 했던 마지막 말이 더 신경 쓰였으니까.
268|
269|‘약점까지 알려 주다니.’
270|
271|이런 황당한 짓거리를 벌이는 이유는 하나뿐이었다.
272|
273|스스로 압도적인 강자라 자부하기에 보일 수 있는 자만.
274|
275|그리고 놈은, 서천마군은 자만을 여유로 보이게 할 정도의 강자다.
276|
277|“제기랄.”
278|
279|크게 심호흡한 나는 착 가라앉은 시선으로 서천마군을 노려봤다.
280|
281|“병문안 온 셈치고 그냥 돌아가면 안 되겠지?”
282|
283|“그건 곤란하네. 자네들은 둘째치고 가져가야 할 물건이 있거든.”
284|
285|“물건?”
286|
287|서천마군은 대답 대신 질문을 던졌다.
288|
289|“이번에는 노부가 묻지. 투항하지 않겠나? 평화롭게.”
290|
291|“자살해 주면 안 될까. 평화롭게.”
292|
293|“그럼 답은 하나밖에 없군.”
294|
295|삼십여 장의 거리.
296|
297|허공에서 나와 서천마군의 시선이 부딪친 그 순간.
298|
299|쐐액, 쉬익!
300|
301|우리는 누가 먼저랄 것도 없이 손을 뻗었다.
302|
303|아니, 적어도 출수에 있어서만큼은 내가 더 빨랐다.
304|
305|다만 서천마군이 쏘아 보낸 지풍(指風)이, 내가 날린 비수보다 한발 앞서 목표에 도달했을 뿐이었다.
306|
307|‘후발선제(後發先制).’
308|
309|머릿속에 붉은색의 경고등이 켜졌다. 동시에 날 선 감각이 주위의 모든 것을 받아들였다.
310|
311|보이지 않는 무형의 지풍. 그러나 다가오는 기운이 똑똑히 느껴졌다. 그건 태을무정검 황보엄을 상대하며 터득한 새로운 감각이었다.
312|

## Adjudicator rules

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)
* a rebuilt joke whose comic machine BASE already has (`얼마나 …는지 …겠다` must stay a simple exaggeration: “snored so loudly even my mother in Ilsan probably heard him,” not “You had to wonder how loudly…”)
* dropped image, attitude, or timing
* SOL replaces an established project rendering, System label, or Markdown convention with an unsupported synonym
* SOL stamps `hyung` (or another kinship title) onto every narrative name when BASE already uses the name and the Korean `형` is ordinary reference, not a vocative or a topical joke (`진호 형` → Jinho in narration)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## `REPAIR` only when both fail

Example: `겹경사가 따로 없다` means two good things **together** (double blessing). `따로` is not “separate.” If BASE says “entirely separate stroke of luck” and SOL says “unexpected windfall,” `REPAIR` to stacked luck.

Do not `REPAIR` a working SOL line. Do not invent a third style because you prefer it.

For `REPAIR`, write the smallest complete replacement needed for that hunk. It must be natural English and fully source-faithful.

## Glossary

Korean **keys** are binding unless the source uses that string in a different ordinary-language sense. Glossary **English** is not a license for a calque (`presiding chair`). If SOL is a natural recast of the same sense, keep SOL.

Return exactly one JSON object and no Markdown fence or prose:

Reasons must name the veto, or say that SOL keeps sense and voice. Do not merely say one version is "better" or "more natural" without stating what changed.

Keep reasons brief. Do not adjudicate unchanged passages. Do not call tools.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.

[P163]
My speed lay beyond anything he had imagined—far beyond the limits of a Peak master.

[P164]
*Stamina, Strength, Agility. And the Flamefire Path.*

[P165]
I poured everything into a single step. I erased the distance and tore through the air.

[P166]
The fire dragon crouched within my qi sea spread its wings and soared. White Flame’s transparent spearhead became the dragon’s claw, plunging toward my enemy.

[P167]
*Heavenly Strike.*

[P168]
Kraaaaaash!

[P169]
* * *

[P170]
Rumble-rumble-rumble!

[P171]
A tremendous tremor swept through the ground.

[P172]
As if to attest to the ferocity of the fighting, the corpses of enemies and allies piled together in tangled heaps collapsed.

[P173]
The pavilion shook as though struck by an earthquake. Even those swinging weapons at one another staggered as they momentarily lost their balance.

[P174]
“An earthquake! It’s an earthquake!”

[P175]
“Damn it, why now…?”

[P176]
An earthquake was a calamity no human strength could stop.

[P177]
The tremor lasted only a moment, but it was enough to fill everyone with fear.

[P178]
Everyone except the two men facing each other in the ruined Family Head’s Hall of the Sichuan Tang Clan.

[P179]
“Ha-ha-ha-ha-ha!”

[P180]
The First Fiend threw back his head and roared with laughter, then turned toward Cheongpung.

[P181]
“You felt that just now, didn’t you?”

[P182]
Cheongpung nodded, looking dazed.

[P183]
“Yes.”

[P184]
Of course he had. The tremor had been an immense wave of qi, powerful enough to be felt from hundreds of yards away.

[P185]
The First Fiend continued with a sneer.

[P186]
“It seems the Demon Lord has finally made up his mind. Heh-heh.”

[P187]
“I know. It’s really amazing.”

[P188]
“He has finally cast aside his last shred of mercy and embraced killing intent. Neither the Fire King nor that disciple of his will survive. Do you understand what that means?”

[P189]
“Yes. My Benefactor really is amazing.”

[P190]
“Now that there’s no longer any need to concern ourselves with the Blood Lord’s wishes, I won’t show you any mercy either—what?”

[P191]
The First Fiend paused and frowned.

[P192]
He couldn’t begin to understand what the greenhorn before him had just said.

[P193]
“Your Benefactor? You mean the Fire King’s disciple?”

[P194]
But Cheongpung’s next words were not directed at the First Fiend.

[P195]
In fact, none of his answers had been directed at him from the start.

[P196]
A quiet murmur slipped from Cheongpung’s lips.

[P197]
“At first, I thought I was far ahead of him. But before I knew it, he’d already come this far…”

[P198]
Cheongpung gazed toward the distant source of the tremor, his eyes shining with joy and ruefulness.

[P199]
No one else in the Sichuan Tang Clan could have guessed the truth—not even the First Fiend standing before him.

[P200]
But Cheongpung knew.

[P201]
“There’s no doubt. That was my Benefactor.”

[P202]
Cheongpung had been happy on Huashan, but he had also been lonely.

[P203]
The beautiful scenery, the animals he could play with, and even the grandfather he revered more than anyone else could not fill a certain emptiness within him.

[P204]
*“There are many young prodigies your age in the Murim. The Ten Dragons and Phoenixes are the best among them.”*

[P205]
*“Hmm. Then are the Ten Dragons and Phoenixes stronger than me?”*

[P206]
*“Huh? What kind of question is that? Of course you’re—”*

[P207]
*“Grandpa?”*

[P208]
*“Ahem. Of course you’re still lacking, Pung.”*

[P209]
*“Gasp! Really?”*

[P210]
*“O-Of course! The world is vast, and there are many masters. So you must continue devoting yourself to your martial arts. Understood?”*

[P211]
*“Yeees…”*

[P212]
At the thoughtless remark his grandfather had let slip, the unfamiliar emotion nestled in one corner of Cheongpung’s heart grew stronger.

[P213]
Only later did he learn its name.

[P214]
Competitive pride.

[P215]
*Which of us is stronger?*

[P216]
He wanted to find out. He wanted to pit his martial arts against theirs and spend time with them.

[P217]

[P218]
*“If it wouldn’t be too much trouble, may I have one candied hawthorn skewer?”*[^1]

[P219]
*“…Mujin. Give him one.”*

[P220]
That was Cheongpung’s first meeting with Jin Taekyung.

[P221]
His Benefactor in name, his friend in truth—and now, his one and only true rival.

[P222]
A gentle smile touched Cheongpung’s lips.

[P223]
“I know. My Benefactor feels the same way I do.”

[P224]
“…!”

[P225]
Flames blazed in the First Fiend’s eyes.

[P226]

[P227]
“You little bastard…”

[P228]
The First Fiend raised his twin axes, their blades caked with scraps of human flesh.

[P229]
Then he saw what was happening before him and froze like a statue.

[P230]
Swooshhh.

[P231]
A wind was blowing.

[P232]
A scarlet wind of qi flowed from Cheongpung’s body, slid down his wrist, and streamed into his sword.

[P233]
It passed over the plum blossom engraved upon the hilt, coiled around the blade, and finally bloomed into a single crimson plum blossom.

[P234]
Crackle-crackle-crackle!

[P235]
A halo of light, more brilliant and destructive than anything else.

[P236]
A stunned whisper escaped the First Fiend’s lips as he stared at the impossible sight.

[P237]
“…Sword Force.”

[P238]
The creation of the greatest martial artists. Proof that its wielder had reached the exalted realm of Supreme Peak.

[P239]
Yet the twenty-three-year-old young man wore an innocent smile utterly unlike that of some exalted master.

[P240]
“Shall we begin?”

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)
* a rebuilt joke whose comic machine BASE already has (`얼마나 …는지 …겠다` must stay a simple exaggeration: “snored so loudly even my mother in Ilsan probably heard him,” not “You had to wonder how loudly…”)
* dropped image, attitude, or timing
* SOL replaces an established project rendering, System label, or Markdown convention with an unsupported synonym
* SOL stamps `hyung` (or another kinship title) onto every narrative name when BASE already uses the name and the Korean `형` is ordinary reference, not a vocative or a topical joke (`진호 형` → Jinho in narration)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## `REPAIR` only when both fail

Example: `겹경사가 따로 없다` means two good things **together** (double blessing). `따로` is not “separate.” If BASE says “entirely separate stroke of luck” and SOL says “unexpected windfall,” `REPAIR` to stacked luck.

Do not `REPAIR` a working SOL line. Do not invent a third style because you prefer it.

For `REPAIR`, write the smallest complete replacement needed for that hunk. It must be natural English and fully source-faithful.

Korean **keys** are binding unless the source uses that string in a different ordinary-language sense. Glossary **English** is not a license for a calque (`presiding chair`). If SOL is a natural recast of the same sense, keep SOL.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.

# Adjudication Task — Chapter 357

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃357화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|평온한 표정과 걸음걸이. 깨끗한 황색 장삼.
  6|
  7|그는 홀로 이질적인 존재였고, 사천당문을 가득 메운 죽음의 기운이 범접할 수 있는 유일한 사람이었다.
  8|
  9|“기껏해야 한 줌밖에 안 되는 놈들이다. 밀어붙여라!”
 10|
 11|“끝까지 싸워라. 우리는 대 사천당문이다!”
 12|
 13|와아아아!
 14|
 15|지축을 떨어 울리는 거대한 함성과 함께 두 개의 파도가 부딪쳤다. 비명과 함성이 뒤섞이고 자욱한 피 안개가 맺혀 간다.
 16|
 17|목숨을 도외시한 치열한 전투. 그만큼 승패가 갈리는 것 또한 순식간이었다.
 18|
 19|“포위하라! 단 한 놈도 살려 두어서는 안 된다!”
 20|
 21|“크아아악!”
 22|
 23|흑의(黑衣)로 이루어진 검은 파도가 녹색 파도를 집어삼켰다.
 24|
 25|파도가 휩쓴 자리에 포말처럼 남은 것은 녹의(綠衣)를 걸친 시신들이었다.
 26|
 27|백여 장 밖에서 이 모든 상황을 바라보던 그, 서천마군이 문득 입을 열었다.
 28|
 29|“끝났군.”
 30|
 31|물러서지 않고 맞서는 결기는 존중할 만하나, 애당초 중과부적(衆寡不敵)의 싸움이었다.
 32|
 33|사천당문의 근간이라 할 수 있는 독과 암기마저 제대로 힘을 발휘하지 못하는 상황.
 34|
 35|전투는, 아니 이 전쟁은 암천의 승리다.
 36|
 37|“약속은 지키지 못할 것 같군. 미안하네, 당 가주.”
 38|
 39|인간은 절박할수록 판단력이 흐려지는 법. 당사독도 예외는 아니었다.
 40|
 41|당가의 명맥을 잇게 해 준다는 조건으로 원하던 대답을 얻어 낸 서천마군이 취한 행동은 간단하고, 잔인했다.
 42|
 43|당장 목숨을 끊는 대신 사천당문이 내려다보이는 언덕 위 나무에 그를 앉혀 놓은 것이다.
 44|
 45|숨이 끊길 때까지 자신의 가문이 멸망하는 것을 지켜볼 수 있도록.
 46|
 47|“모든 것은 천주의 뜻대로.”
 48|
 49|투둑, 투두둑.
 50|
 51|어느새 빗방울을 떨어트리는 하늘을 바라보던 서천마군이 신형을 돌렸다.
 52|
 53|시커먼 아가리를 쩍 벌리고 있는 동혈(洞穴) 입구. 쓰러진 화로 옆에 웬 곱사등이 노인 하나가 눈을 부릅뜬 채 죽어 있었다.
 54|
 55|서천마군의 흥미를 끈 것은 노인의 몸에 새겨진 상흔이었다.
 56|
 57|‘흑혈검법(黑血劍法).’
 58|
 59|흑혈검법은 암천의 무인들에게만 허락된 검법.
 60|
 61|선객들의 정체를 알아차린 서천마군은 지하로 향하는 돌계단을 따라 내려갔다.
 62|
 63|계단에는 핏물과 진흙이 뒤섞인 발자국들이 선명하게 남아 있었다. 적어도 스물 이상의 수하들이 그보다 앞서 이곳을 방문했음이 틀림없었다.
 64|
 65|그리고 아마도…….
 66|
 67|‘모두 죽었겠지.’
 68|
 69|내려간 흔적은 있어도 올라온 흔적은 없다.
 70|
 71|지하 뇌옥에 진입하자 짐작은 확신으로 변했다.
 72|
 73|피로 얼룩진 인생을 살았던 서천마군이다. 어두컴컴한 복도에 남아 있는 전투의 열기, 악취에 덮인 비릿한 혈향(血香)을 느낄 수 있었다.
 74|
 75|누구의 짓일까, 서천마군은 벽면에 튄 미세한 핏방울을 보며 생각했다.
 76|
 77|‘솜씨가 좋군. 제대로 된 저항도 하지 못하고 당했어.’
 78|
 79|사천당문이 풍전등화의 위기에 처한 지금, 당문의 고수들이 외인들을 지키기 위해 이곳에 있을 리는 없다.
 80|
 81|당사독의 말이 사실이라면 지금 지하 뇌옥에 남아 있는 자는 셋.
 82|
 83|신의는 있으나 마나 한 전력이고 화왕 적천강은 의식을 회복하지도 못했으니, 남은 사람은 한 명뿐이다.
 84|
 85|‘산서잠룡 진태경.’
 86|
 87|문득 혈주가 진태경을 두고 했던 말이 생각났다.
 88|
 89|천하에서 가장 건방지고, 끈질기며, 간이 배 밖으로 튀어나온 어린놈.
 90|
 91|어째서인지 그는 제 팔을 잘라 낸 검성이나 화왕보다 진태경을 더 죽이고 싶어 했다.
 92|
 93|‘혈주를 상대로 살아남을 정도의 실력은 있다, 이건가.’
 94|
 95|그러나 진태경에게 두 번의 요행은 없을 것이다.
 96|
 97|검성은 이 자리에 없고 화왕 역시 전투 불능의 상태.
 98|
 99|서천마군은 독 안에 든 쥐새끼들을 손쉽게 붙잡아 귀환할 생각이었다.
100|
101|‘놈들이 가진 만독지환과 함께 말이지.’
102|
103|철벅, 철벅.
104|
105|여유롭게 걸음을 옮기던 서천마군의 신형이 우뚝 멈췄다.
106|
107|어느새 천장으로부터 이어진 단단한 돌벽이 그를 가로막고 있었다.
108|
109|“허, 참. 복잡하게도 지어 놨군.”
110|
111|물끄러미 벽을 바라보던 서천마군이 손을 그러모았다. 검붉은 안개가 그의 팔을 휘감으며 주먹을 감싼다.
112|
113|고오오오옹.
114|
115|모든 것은 순식간에 일어났다.
116|
117|기의 발현, 압축, 그리고 폭발. 권강(拳罡)의 앞을 가로막을 수 있는 것은 아무것도 없었다.
118|
119|쿠구구구궁!
120|
121|부수고, 무너지고, 흔들린다.
122|
123|강대한 기의 집약체는 일직선으로 뻗어 나가며 수십 개의 벽을 관통했다. 천장에서는 종유석이 우박처럼 쏟아져 내렸고 자욱한 먼지구름이 피어올랐다.
124|
125|‘한결 낫군.’
126|
127|다음 순간.
128|
129|자신이 만든 광경을 바라보던 서천마군이 문득 입을 열었다.
130|
131|“이만 나오지 그러나.”
132|
133|대답 대신 돌아온 것은 강렬한 파공성이었다.
134|
135|퍼엉!
136|
137|갈라지는 먼지구름 사이, 자신의 목을 향해 날아든 비수를 낚아챈 서천마군이 빙긋 웃었다.
138|
139|“자네가 진태경인가?”
140|
141|“알면서 뭘 물어.”
142|
143|저벅, 저벅.
144|
145|먼지구름을 헤치며 걸어온 훤칠한 체구의 청년, 진태경이 덤덤한 눈빛으로 서천마군을 응시했다.
146|
147|
148|
149|* * *
150|
151|
152|
153|나는 덤덤해 보이려고 애썼다.
154|
155|싸움은 기세가 절반은 먹고 들어간다. 상대가 나보다 약해 보인다고 해서 방심하면 안 되고, 강해 보인다고 해서 주눅 들어서도 안 된다.
156|
157|특히…… 지금처럼 진짜배기 강자를 만났을 때는 더더욱.
158|
159|‘뭐 이런 괴물 같은 놈이.’
160|
161|내심 혀를 내두르며 눈앞의 중년인을 바라봤다.
162|
163|모세가 지팡이로 바다를 갈랐다면, 그는 일권(一拳)으로 지하 뇌옥에 또 다른 길을 만들었다.
164|
165|그뿐인가, 미소 띤 얼굴로 서 있는 모습은 평온 그 자체였다.
166|
167|‘풍기는 냄새 자체가 달라.’
168|
169|혈주가 대놓고 미친놈이었다면, 눈앞의 이 중년인은 존재 자체만으로도 위험한 인간이다.
170|
171|둘의 무공은 엇비슷할지 몰라도 종류가 달랐다.
172|
173|“자네 얘기는 많이 들었네. 듣던 대로 재밌는 청년이로군.”
174|
175|나는 백염(白炎)의 창날을 비스듬하게 늘어트리며 대꾸했다.
176|
177|“내가 또 한 재미 하지.”
178|
179|“예의가 없다고도 하더군.”
180|

[P45]

Gooooooong.

Whoosh!

“…!”

“……”

“You’re the Western Heaven Demon Lord, aren’t you?”

[P123]
“What?”

[P124]

[P125]
“…!”

[P129]

[P130]

[P132]

[P134]

[P135]

[P136]
“Damn it.”

[P137]

[P138]

“Something?”

[P158]

[P159]
Whoosh!

Kraaaaaash!

[P199]

[P200]
“There’s no doubt. It’s my Benefactor.”

[P202]

[P203]
*“There are many young prodigies your age in the Murim. The Ten Dragons and Phoenixes are the best among them.”*

[P204]
*“Um. Are those Ten Dragons and Phoenixes stronger than me?”*

[P205]
*“Huh? What kind of question is that? Of course you, Pung, are—”*

[P206]
*“Grandpa?”*

[P207]
*“Ahem. Of course you’re lacking.”*

[P208]
*“Gasp! Really?”*

[P209]
*“O-Of course! The world is vast, and there are many masters. So you’ll have to keep working hard at your martial arts from now on, right?”*

[P210]
*“Yeees…”*

[P212]

[P213]
Competitive pride.

[P214]
*Which of us is stronger?*

[P215]

[P218]
*“...Mujin. Give him one.”*

[P220]
A person who was his Benefactor in name and his friend in truth. And now, his only true rival.

[P221]
A gentle smile formed at the corner of his mouth.

[P222]
“I know. I know my Benefactor thinks the same way I do.”

[P223]
“…!”

[P225]

[P226]
“You little bastard…”

Swooshhh.

[P233]
Crackle-crackle-crackle!

[P235]

[P236]

[P238]
Yet the twenty-three-year-old young man’s face wore an innocent smile wholly unsuited to a great martial artist.

[P239]
“So, shall we begin?”

[P110]
The good news was that Cheongpung was alive and the Blood Lord wasn’t here. The bad news was that if I lost this fight, we’d all be attending a group get-together with him.

[P111]
The odds that we’d share a bottle of soju over grilled intestines and then go our separate ways were close to zero.

[P112]
*The odds that I’ll become the grilled intestines instead are probably around fifty percent.*

[P113]
The other fifty percent was the chance I’d end up as grilled tripe.

[P114]
Damn it. Just thinking about it was making my mouth water.

[P115]
I swallowed dryly and looked the middle-aged man up and down.

[P116]
A man who could call the Blood Lord, presumably one of Dark Heaven’s highest-ranking figures, an acquaintance. A man who could unleash that much destructive power with a single punch.

[P117]
A title came to mind.

[P118]
“You’re the Western Heaven Demon Lord, aren’t you?”

[P119]
“Ah, come to think of it, I haven’t introduced myself yet. It’s a pleasure to meet you.”

[P120]
Pleasure, my ass.

[P121]
I stared at the Western Heaven Demon Lord’s two perfectly intact arms.

[P122]
“I heard you only had one arm.”

[P123]
“That was true until ten days ago.”

[P124]
“What?”

[P125]
“I had another attached. It wasn’t originally mine, so it still doesn’t move quite as well as I’d like. If you intend to try something, aim for my left arm.”

[P126]
“…!”

[P127]
What the hell was this guy?

[P128]
Even if some kind of suturing operation was possible, he had replaced an arm as if it were a computer component.

[P129]
Aside from the subtle difference in skin tone, it moved perfectly naturally.

[P130]
*Is that even possible? And in only ten days?*

[P131]
I couldn’t make any sense of it, but I had to set my shock and questions aside for now.

[P132]
His last remark bothered me even more.

[P133]
*He even told me his weakness.*

[P134]
There could only be one reason for something that absurd.

[P135]
It was the kind of arrogance only someone certain of his overwhelming strength could display.

[P136]
And the Western Heaven Demon Lord was strong enough to make arrogance look like composure.

[P137]
“Damn it.”

[P138]
I drew a deep breath and fixed him with a cold, level stare.

[P139]
“Can’t you just pretend you came to visit a patient and turn around?”

[P140]
“That would be difficult. Setting you aside, there’s something I need to take with me.”

[P141]
“Something?”

[P142]
Instead of answering, the Western Heaven Demon Lord posed a question of his own.

[P143]
“Then allow this old man to ask. Will you surrender peacefully?”

[P144]
“Could you kill yourself peacefully?”

[P145]
“Then there’s only one answer.”

[P146]
Roughly a hundred yards separated us.

[P147]
The instant our gazes collided across that distance—

[P148]
Whoosh! Swish!

[P149]
We both moved at once.

[P150]
No. When it came to launching our attacks, at least, I was faster.

[P151]
It was just that the Finger Qi fired by the Western Heaven Demon Lord reached its target before my dagger did.

[P152]
*Striking second, hitting first.*

[P153]
A red warning light flashed in my head. At the same time, my sharpened senses took in everything around me.

[P154]
The Finger Qi was formless and invisible, yet I could clearly feel its approach. It was a new sense I had acquired while fighting Hwangbo Eom, the Taeeul Merciless Sword.

[P155]
*Now!*

[P156]
I twisted my head and shot forward. Something faster than a bullet grazed my ear.

[P157]
The Western Heaven Demon Lord watched me with open surprise.

[P158]
“To evade a Ghost Prison Finger at eighty percent power… You certainly have a talent for surprising people as well—”

[P159]
“Yeah, Ghost Prison Finger.”

[P160]
Whoosh!

[P161]
The Western Heaven Demon Lord’s voice cut off.

[P162]
Within that slowed instant, his widening pupils reflected me closing in right before his eyes.

[P163]
My speed lay beyond anything he had imagined—far beyond the limits of a Peak master.

[P164]
*Stamina, Strength, Agility. And the Flamefire Path.*

[P165]
I poured everything into a single step. I erased the distance and tore through the air.

[P166]
The fire dragon crouched within my qi sea spread its wings and soared. White Flame’s transparent spearhead became the dragon’s claw, plunging toward my enemy.

[P167]
*Heavenly Strike.*

[P168]
Kraaaaaash!

[P169]
* * *

[P170]
Rumble-rumble-rumble!

[P171]
A tremendous tremor swept through the ground.

[P172]
As if to attest to the ferocity of the fighting, the corpses of enemies and allies piled together in tangled heaps collapsed.

[P173]
The pavilion shook as though struck by an earthquake. Even those swinging weapons at one another staggered as they momentarily lost their balance.

[P174]
“An earthquake! It’s an earthquake!”

[P175]
“Damn it, why now…?”

[P176]
An earthquake was a calamity no human strength could stop.

[P177]
The tremor lasted only a moment, but it was enough to fill everyone with fear.

[P178]
Everyone except the two men facing each other in the ruined Family Head’s Hall of the Sichuan Tang Clan.

[P179]
“Ha-ha-ha-ha-ha!”

[P180]
The First Fiend threw back his head and roared with laughter, then turned toward Cheongpung.

[P181]
“You felt that just now, didn’t you?”

[P182]
Cheongpung nodded, looking dazed.

[P183]
“Yes.”

[P184]
Of course he had. The tremor had been an immense wave of qi, powerful enough to be felt from hundreds of yards away.

[P185]
The First Fiend continued with a sneer.

[P186]
“It seems the Demon Lord has finally made up his mind. Heh-heh.”

[P187]
“I know. It’s really amazing.”

[P188]
“He has finally cast aside his last shred of mercy and embraced killing intent. Neither the Fire King nor that disciple of his will survive. Do you understand what that means?”

[P189]
“Yes. My Benefactor really is amazing.”

[P190]
“Now that there’s no longer any need to concern ourselves with the Blood Lord’s wishes, I won’t show you any mercy either—what?”

[P191]
The First Fiend paused and frowned.

[P192]
He couldn’t begin to understand what the greenhorn before him had just said.

[P193]
“Your Benefactor? You mean the Fire King’s disciple?”

[P194]
But Cheongpung’s next words were not directed at the First Fiend.

[P195]
In fact, none of his answers had been directed at him from the start.

[P196]
A quiet murmur slipped from Cheongpung’s lips.

[P197]
“At first, I thought I was far ahead of him. But before I knew it, he’d already come this far…”

[P198]
Cheongpung gazed toward the distant source of the tremor, his eyes shining with joy and ruefulness.

[P199]
No one else in the Sichuan Tang Clan could have guessed the truth—not even the First Fiend standing before him.

[P200]
But Cheongpung knew.

[P201]
“There’s no doubt. That was my Benefactor.”

[P202]
Cheongpung had been happy on Huashan, but he had also been lonely.

[P203]
The beautiful scenery, the animals he could play with, and even the grandfather he revered more than anyone else could not fill a certain emptiness within him.

[P204]
*“There are many young prodigies your age in the Murim. The Ten Dragons and Phoenixes are the best among them.”*

[P205]
*“Hmm. Then are the Ten Dragons and Phoenixes stronger than me?”*

[P206]
*“Huh? What kind of question is that? Of course you’re—”*

[P207]
*“Grandpa?”*

[P208]
*“Ahem. Of course you’re still lacking, Pung.”*

[P209]
*“Gasp! Really?”*

[P210]
*“O-Of course! The world is vast, and there are many masters. So you must continue devoting yourself to your martial arts. Understood?”*

[P211]
*“Yeees…”*

[P212]
At the thoughtless remark his grandfather had let slip, the unfamiliar emotion nestled in one corner of Cheongpung’s heart grew stronger.

[P213]
Only later did he learn its name.

[P214]
Competitive pride.

[P215]
*Which of us is stronger?*

[P216]
He wanted to find out. He wanted to pit his martial arts against theirs and spend time with them.

[P217]
And so Cheongpung left Huashan and ventured into the world. Then, on a sunny winter day, he met him.

[P218]
*“If it wouldn’t be too much trouble, may I have one candied hawthorn skewer?”*[^1]

[P219]
*“…Mujin. Give him one.”*

[P220]
That was Cheongpung’s first meeting with Jin Taekyung.

[P221]
His Benefactor in name, his friend in truth—and now, his one and only true rival.

[P222]
A gentle smile touched Cheongpung’s lips.

[P223]
“I know. My Benefactor feels the same way I do.”

[P224]
“…!”

[P225]
Flames blazed in the First Fiend’s eyes.

[P226]
This greenhorn would have died long ago if not for the Western Heaven Demon Lord’s orders, yet he dared to ignore him. That alone had sealed his fate.

[P227]
“You little bastard…”

[P228]
The First Fiend raised his twin axes, their blades caked with scraps of human flesh.

[P229]
Then he saw what was happening before him and froze like a statue.

[P230]
Swooshhh.

[P231]
A wind was blowing.

[P232]
A scarlet wind of qi flowed from Cheongpung’s body, slid down his wrist, and streamed into his sword.

[P233]
It passed over the plum blossom engraved upon the hilt, coiled around the blade, and finally bloomed into a single crimson plum blossom.

[P234]
Crackle-crackle-crackle!

[P235]
A halo of light, more brilliant and destructive than anything else.

[P236]
A stunned whisper escaped the First Fiend’s lips as he stared at the impossible sight.

[P237]
“…Sword Force.”

[P238]
The creation of the greatest martial artists. Proof that its wielder had reached the exalted realm of Supreme Peak.

[P239]
Yet the twenty-three-year-old young man wore an innocent smile utterly unlike that of some exalted master.

[P240]
“Shall we begin?”

[P241]
[^1]: Candied hawthorn skewers are a traditional snack made by coating skewered hawthorn fruit in hardened sugar.

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)
* a rebuilt joke whose comic machine BASE already has (`얼마나 …는지 …겠다` must stay a simple exaggeration: “snored so loudly even my mother in Ilsan probably heard him,” not “You had to wonder how loudly…”)
* dropped image, attitude, or timing
* SOL replaces an established project rendering, System label, or Markdown convention with an unsupported synonym
* SOL stamps `hyung` (or another kinship title) onto every narrative name when BASE already uses the name and the Korean `형` is ordinary reference, not a vocative or a topical joke (`진호 형` → Jinho in narration)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## `REPAIR` only when both fail

Example: `겹경사가 따로 없다` means two good things **together** (double blessing). `따로` is not “separate.” If BASE says “entirely separate stroke of luck” and SOL says “unexpected windfall,” `REPAIR` to stacked luck.

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.
